extracted.intended_audience: machine_learning researchers, model developers, and AI safety researchers / practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluation dimensions used to measure capabilities, limitations, and safety of a large multimodal language+vision model (GPT-4), including benchmark performance, scaling behavior, factuality, calibration, safety/refusal behavior, and evaluation methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exam performance (simulated professional & academic exams)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulate the conditions and scoring of real human exams (multiple-choice and free-response, images included where required) and report final score and estimated percentile among test takers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run variants removing any questions seen in training and report the lower score of the two; combine multiple-choice and free-response scores using publicly available methodologies for each exam; estimate percentiles (be conservative and report lower bound); perform contamination checks and report methodology (see Appendix A and C). Examples: Uniform Bar Exam, LSAT, SAT, GRE, AP exams; report per-exam scoring and percentiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark performance on standard NLP / ML datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure task-specific performance (accuracy, F1, pass_rate, etc.) on established benchmarks such as MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC, WinoGrande, HumanEval, DROP, GSM-8K and compare to prior LMs and SOTA systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use few-shot prompting when appropriate; for multiple-choice present all options and ask model to choose a letter; for HumanEval use pass_rate (ability to synthesize correct Python functions); for DROP report F1. Run contamination checks to exclude benchmark data that appears in training (exclude contaminated datasets from reported results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictable scaling & loss prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether infrastructure and optimization methods allow accurate prediction of final loss and some capability metrics (e.g., HumanEval pass rate) from models trained with far less compute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit a scaling law (e.g., L(C) = a C^b + c) using smaller models and predict final loss for large runs; register predictions before training completes; evaluate prediction accuracy (e.g., power law fits to smaller models accurately predicting GPT-4's final loss).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability prediction on interpretable metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Predict more interpretable capability metrics (e.g., pass_rate on HumanEval) by extrapolating performance from smaller models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split problems into difficulty buckets based on smaller-model performance, restrict to problems where low pass rates are estimable, register predictions prior to full training, and compare observed vs predicted pass rates across buckets; note some buckets (easiest/hardest) may under/over-perform predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contamination checks / training-set overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify and report whether evaluation data (exams/benchmarks) appear in the pre-training or fine-tuning data and account for this in reported results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each exam/benchmark run a contamination check and, when contamination is found, run a variant with contaminated questions removed and report the more conservative (lower) score. Exclude datasets (e.g., BIG-bench) if contamination is discovered and cannot be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual input capability (multimodal evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the model's ability to accept arbitrarily interlaced text and images as input and produce text outputs across domains such as documents, photographs, diagrams, and screenshots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design image+text prompts for tasks requiring vision; apply standard test-time techniques (few-shot, chain-of-thought) and compare to text-only performance; provide representative example prompts and assess quality qualitatively and quantitatively on narrow vision benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to follow user intent (human preference / alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how often responses from the model are preferred by humans compared to baselines (e.g., GPT-3.5), indicating alignment with user intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect real user prompts, sample one response per model, have human labelers judge which response matches the user's intent (labelers blind to model identity), filter out disallowed/sensitive/common trivial prompts; report percentage preference (e.g., GPT-4 responses preferred on 70.2% of prompts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factuality / hallucination rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how frequently the model generates incorrect facts or reasoning errors ('hallucinations') using adversarially-designed factuality evaluations and public datasets like TruthfulQA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run internal adversarial factuality evaluations across topics and report accuracy; compare pre-trained vs post-trained (RLHF) performance; sample-by-sample inspection (OpenAI Evals) can be used; quantify improvement relative to prior models (e.g., 19 percentage point improvement vs GPT-3.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration (confidence vs accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure whether the model's predicted confidence (logprob) correlates with actual accuracy across confidence bins, report expected calibration error (ECE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce calibration plots for pre-trained and post-trained models; note RLHF/post-training can degrade calibration (increase ECE) even while improving other metrics; report ECE and visual calibration curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias and harmful representation (fairness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess biases in outputs (stereotypes, demeaning content) and characterize harms of representation across sensitive attributes (race, religion, disability, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use curated prompt suites that probe for harmful or biased content (examples in appendix), compare early vs post-training model responses, and report residual risks and examples; apply mitigation strategies and document remaining limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety / refusal behavior on disallowed and sensitive prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the model's tendency to respond to disallowed requests (illicit instructions, violent wrongdoing, etc.) and its handling of sensitive but allowed prompts (medical/self-harm) according to policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use red-team prompts and expert-created safety-relevant prompts; classify outputs into desired refusal styles vs undesired (evasive/rambling) vs disallowed content vs safe non-refusal; report incorrect behavior rates and relative improvements (e.g., decrease in responding to disallowed content by 82% compared to GPT-3.5; 29% improvement on sensitive requests adherence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxicity / harmful content generation rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify the rate at which the model produces toxic or abusive language on standard datasets (e.g., RealToxicityPrompts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run model generations on toxicity benchmark inputs and report percent toxic outputs (e.g., GPT-4: 0.73% toxic vs GPT-3.5: 6.48%); use these metrics to track progress and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to jailbreaks and adversarial system messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how difficult it is to elicit forbidden behavior via adversarial prompts, system messages, or other jailbreak techniques and characterize remaining vulnerabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document examples of jailbreaks that still work, quantify increased difficulty vs prior models, and recommend deployment-time mitigations (monitoring, iterative improvement pipeline) since jailbreaks remain possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-assisted safety pipeline & rule-based reward models (RBRMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use model-derived classifiers (zero-shot GPT-4 classifiers) combined with human-written rubrics to provide reward signals during RLHF fine-tuning to steer behavior toward desired refusals and non-refusals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide RBRM inputs: prompt (optional), policy output, and a human-written rubric; classify outputs into categories (desired refusal, undesired refusal, disallowed content, safe non-refusal) and use as additional reward signal; tune RBRM weights and provide additional SFT data targeting desired behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adversarial testing with domain experts (red-teaming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage over 50 domain experts across relevant risk domains (biorisk, cybersecurity, long-term alignment, etc.) to adversarially test model behavior and inform mitigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expert findings to collect training data for refusals and other mitigations (e.g., data to improve refusals on dangerous chemical synthesis); document example interactions and responses that demonstrate improved refusals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation methodology transparency & conservative reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Document evaluation protocols (prompting style, few-shot/chain-of-thought usage, dataset splits, contamination handling) and adopt conservative reporting practices (report lower bound percentiles, exclude contaminated items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each benchmark/exam provide prompt templates, few-shot examples, whether chain-of-thought was used, and how final scores/percentiles were computed; when training-set overlap exists report both with and without contaminated items and conservatively report lower values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess model performance on translated variants of benchmarks (e.g., MMLU) across multiple languages, including low-resource languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate benchmarks (e.g., via Azure Translate), run few-shot evaluations in each language, compare against English baselines and prior models, and report language-wise accuracy; GPT-4 showed improved performance in many languages (surpassing English-language SOTA in many cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-offs introduced by post-training (RLHF) steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Document how post-training alignment improves some behaviors (e.g., adherence to policy, refusal quality) while potentially harming others (e.g., calibration), and report both pre-trained and post-trained metrics where informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare pre-trained and RLHF/post-trained model behavior on tasks such as multiple-choice performance (may be similar), factuality, calibration, and refusal behavior; present calibration curves and accuracy differences to illustrate trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prompting techniques (few-shot, chain-of-thought)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the effectiveness of prompting strategies (few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought) for eliciting higher performance across tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating benchmarks, specify the prompting strategy used (e.g., few-shot, chain-of-thought) and show performance differences; e.g., use chain-of-thought on GSM-8K and few-shot on MMLU/HumanEval where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open, inspectable evals & per-sample analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide tools and frameworks (e.g., OpenAI Evals) to create and run benchmarks while inspecting performance sample-by-sample, enabling fine-grained analysis of failures and strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-source or document the eval framework used, encourage diversity of benchmarks over time to capture broader failure modes, and enable auditors to reproduce and inspect evaluation samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-stakes usage guidance and mitigation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Advise caution and require additional protocols (human review, grounding with external context, or avoidance) when using model outputs in high-stakes contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend matching verification/review protocols to the application’s risk profile (e.g., specialized human oversight, external grounding, or disallowing certain high-stakes uses altogether); emphasize limitations like knowledge cutoff and non-learning from experience.
